questions.question: The difference between the simple interest and compound interest on ₹1,000 for 1 year at 20% per annum, compounded half-yearly, is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

P=1000, R=20%, T= 1year

**Formula used:**

SI = (P× R× T)/(100)

A = P(1+(R)/(100))^T

P= Principal

R= Rate of interest

T= Time

A = Amount

**Calculation:**

for compounded half-yearly, the rate gets halved and time gets doubled

⇒ R = 20/2

⇒ R = 10%

⇒ T = 1 × 2

⇒ T = 2 years

For SI

⇒ SI = (P× R× T)/(100)

⇒ SI = (1000×10×2)/(100)

⇒ SI = Rs. 200

For CI

⇒ A = P(1+(R)/(100))^T=1000(1+(10)/(100))²

⇒ A = 1000(1+(1)/(10))²

⇒ A = 1000((11)/(10) × (11)/(10))

⇒ A = Rs. 1210

⇒ I = A - P

⇒ I = 1210-1000

 

⇒ I = Rs. 210

Difference = CI - SI

⇒ 210-200

⇒ Rs.10

**∴ The answer is Rs. 10.**

questions.question: If an increase of 40% is observed on an amount in 4 years at simple interest, what will be the compound interest on ₹80,000 after 4 years at the same rate of interest?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹80,000

Time (t) = 4 years

Simple Interest Increase = 40%

**Formula used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = P × r × t / 100

Amount (A) = P(1 + r/100)t

**Calculation:**

Simple Interest Increase = 40%

⇒ 40 = r × 4 / 100

⇒ r = 40 × 100 / 4

⇒ r = 10%

Now, find compound interest:

Amount (A) = P(1 + r/100)t

A = 80,000(1 + 10/100)⁴

⇒ A = 80,000(1 + 0.1)⁴

⇒ A = 80,000(1.1)⁴

⇒ A = 80,000 × 1.4641

⇒ A = ₹117,128

Compound Interest (CI) = A - P

CI = 117,128 - 80,000

⇒ CI = ₹37,128

**∴ The correct answer is option 2.**

questions.question: There is a 60% increase in an amount in 5 years at simple interest. What will be the compound interest on Rs. 6,250 for two years at the same rate of interest, when the interest is compounded yearly?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A Simple Interest on a particular sum is 60% of the principle in 5 years.

Let P be the principle and R% is the rate of interest p.a.

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest **( S.I ) = ( P× R× T )/ 100**

Where P = Principle, R = Rate of interest, T = time period

Compound Interest **( C.I ) = P(1 + R/100)T – P**

Where P = Principle, R = Rate of interest, T = time period

**Calculations:**

⇒ As from the given formula

 S.I for 5 years = 60%× P = P× R%× 5

⇒ R% = 60% / 5 = 12% ____( 1 )

As 12% = ( +3/25) = 28/25

⇒ C.I = 6250( 1 + 12/100 )² – 6250

(∵ Principle is given = Rs 6250 )

⇒ C.I = 6250 (28/25)² – 6250 = 6250× 784/625 – 6250

( As 28² = 784, 25² = 625 )

**C.I = 7840 – 6250 = Rs 1590**

questions.question: On a sum of money, when invested for 2 years, compound interest and simple interest are ₹300 and ₹250, respectively. For both simple and compound interests the rate of interest per annum is the same, and for compound interest, interest is compounded annually. Find the rate of interest per annum.
questions.solution:
**GIVEN:**

C.I. for 2 years = Rs300 

S.I. for 2 years = Rs250.

Where C.I. = Compound Interest , S.I. = Simple interest 

**Concept Used:**

Difference between C.I. and S.I. for 2 years = (CI - SI)over(SI of one year) × 100

**CALCULATION:**

S.I. for 2 years = Rs250 

Hence, S.I. for 1 year = 250/2 = Rs125.

Now, C.I. for 2 years = Rs300.

Difference between C.I. and S.I. for 2 years = ( 300 -250) = Rs50.

Hence, Required Rate of Interest =( 50/ 125 ) × 100 = 40%.

**∴ The required rate of interest is 40%.**

questions.question: A sum amounts to Rs. 6580 in 2 years and amounts to Rs. 7896 in 3 years on compound interest (compounding annually) at the same rate of interest. What is the annual rate of interest?
questions.solution:
**Calculation:**

If the sum amounts to Rs. 6580 in 2 years and Rs. 7896 in 3 years, the difference (Rs. 7896 - Rs. 6580 = Rs. 1316) would be the interest earned in the third year.

So, the interest for the third year, Rs. 1316, was obtained from the amount that was there at the end of two years, which is Rs. 6580.

Interest for third year = Sum after 2 years × annual interest rate

1316 = 6580 × r

Solving this equation for r gives us:

r = 1316/6580 × 100 = 20%

**So, the annual rate of interest is 20%.**

The simple interest on a certain sum of money for 5 years at the rate of 10% per annum is half the compound interest on Rs. 5,000 for 2 years at the rate of 10% per annum, interest compounded yearly

SI = (P × R × T)/100

CI = P(1 + R/100)T – P

Where, P = Principal, R = Rate, T = Time

**Calculation:**

CI = P(1 + R/100)T – P

⇒ 5000(1 + 10/100)² – 5000

⇒ 5000(110/100)² – 5000

⇒ (5000 × 11/10 × 11/10) – 5000

⇒ Rs. 6050 – 5000

⇒ Rs. 1050

Now,

SI is half the CI = Rs. (1050 × 1/2) = Rs. 525

Now,

SI = (P × R × T)/100

⇒ 525 = (P × 5 × 10)/100

⇒ 525 = 50P/100

⇒ P = Rs. (525 × 100)/50

⇒ P = Rs. 1050

**∴ The sum placed on simple interest is Rs. 1,050**

Time = 2 years

Amount = Principal + Simple Interest

⇒ Sum invested at simple interest = 12050 - y

⇒ (12050 - y) [1 + 1/5] = y × 11/10 × 11/10 

⇒ (12050 - y) × 6/5 = y × 121/100 

⇒ 12050 × 6/5 - y × 6/5 = y × 121/100 

⇒14460 = 121y/100 + 6y/5

⇒ 14460 = (121y + 120y)/100 

⇒ 14460 = 241y/100 

⇒y = (14460 × 100)/241 

⇒ y = 6000 

**∴ The sum invested on compound interest is Rs.6000.**

(121 + 120) units = 12050

⇒ 241 units = 12050

The sum invested on CI = 120 units = 50 × 120

Amount = P(1 + r/100)t

CI = A – P

**Calculation:**

Let Principal be x

SI = (x × 10 × 3)/100

⇒ 3x/10

Now,

Amount = P(1 + r/100)t

⇒ x(1 + 10/100)³

⇒ [x(100 + 10)/100]³

⇒ [x(110/100)³]

⇒ (x × 11/10 × 11/10 × 11/10)

⇒ 1331x/1000

Now,

CI = A – P

⇒ CI = (1331x/1000 – x)

⇒ (1331x – 1000x)/1000

⇒ 331x/1000

The difference between the CI and SI = Rs. 279

⇒ (331x – 300x)/1000 = 279

⇒ 31x/1000 = 279

⇒ x = (9 × 1000)

⇒ Rs. 9000

questions.question: Kalyan invested a sum of ₹12,000 for two years compounded at 5% and 10%, respectively. What is the compound interest (in ₹) at the end of two years?
questions.solution:
**Given:** 

Principal (P) = ₹12,000

First-year interest rate (r1) = 5%

Second-year interest rate (r2) = 10% 

**Calculation:**

A1 = P(1 + r1)

A1 = 12000(1 + 0.05)

A1 = 12000 × 1.05 = ₹12,600

Second Year: For the second year, we use the amount at the end of the first year as the principal.

P2 = A1 (the amount from the first year becomes the principal for the second year)

A2 = P2(1 + r2)

A2 = 12600(1 + 0.1)

A2 = 12600 × 1.1 = ₹13,860

Compound Interest = A2 - P

Compound Interest = 13860 - 12000
